personText: They provide shade along the walk, but not much more for me. Sometimes a frustration when I'm trying to get home and Lily stops to smell each tree.
dogText: Lily loves these along the walk. She will stop to lay down in the grass, smell the roots of the tree, or look up to see if there are any squirrels she can bark at.  In general, I think there are a lot of smells on/associated with the tree that are interesting to her
walkText: They provide shade for Lily, she can get hot on summer walks, also, they break up the monotony of a walk for her with new smells.

dogText: Lily's favorite thing on walks, just very lush green lawns. Sometimes there's a smell on the ground, sometiems, I think it's just soft and she likes laying in it.
walkText: It's not much, but thick, well-kept grass is nice. Often expected for neighborhood walks, but nothing major.

personText: I forget to bring water so this is great for my dog walks
dogText: This is crucial for long Lily walks. So good to keep her energy up.
walkText: It's intentionally meant to support dog walking

imageDescript: This is the perfect halfway spot on our walk, the grass is the softest of the lawns we go through which is why I consider it part of the built environment. It's managed by a local business.
personText: I love the halfway point break where I can just sit with Lily for an extended period of time
dogText: Lily loves this break. She knows when it's coming, rolls on the ground and smells the bushes alongside the building. It's like a mini play break.
walkText: We take long walks, and Lily doesn't often do more than just walk alongside me. However, the vibrant lawn, lots of shade, and dense foliage creates a mini park with a lot of smells that she loves to investigate and run around in before laying down and chilling out.
